clips.text_zh: Bitcoin bull run 今晚就開始。好多 Bitcoin options 今日 4pm EST 到期。有人估計會有個大波動。我更加係準備畀 liquidation 自己，唔係準備贏。靠AI續命，CFD 又再交學費。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: A bull run starts tonight. Many Bitcoin options expire today at 4pm EST. That could create strong short-term price movement. The post presents a bullish Bitcoin view, although no entry price or target is given.
clips.text_en_b2: The Bitcoin bull run could begin tonight, although the post gives no entry price or target. Many options are expiring today at 4 p.m. EST, and traders expect those positions to produce a sharp short-term price movement. Rather than positioning to profit from the move, the author is preparing for liquidation. It’s AI keeping the thread alive, while CFDs are charging another round of tuition.
clips.text_en_c1: The Bitcoin bull run begins tonight, with numerous options contracts expiring at 4 p.m. EST. Such a concentration of expiries could trigger substantial volatility, particularly if traders have positioned themselves heavily in either direction. Although the original post is bullish and treats the expiry as the potential catalyst for a move higher, it provides neither an entry price nor a concrete target. The author also sounds pessimistic about their own prospects, expecting liquidations rather than a profitable outcome. In short, this is a bullish prediction tempered by an unusually realistic sense of risk.
clips.text_en_c2: A Bitcoin bull run could begin tonight, as a substantial concentration of options contracts reaches expiry at 4 p.m. EST. Such a deadline may provoke sharp volatility, with liquidations potentially forcing prices in either direction before the session settles. The underlying view is bullish, yet the poster offers neither an entry price nor a profit target, so conviction remains conspicuously unquantified. Rather than positioning to emerge on the winning side, the trader appears to be bracing for a liquidation event and relying on artificial intelligence to keep the position alive. CFDs, meanwhile, look set to extract another tuition fee, with a prayer emoji lending the wager a distinctly devotional veneer.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post about tonight’s Bitcoin options expiry and a possible bull run.

clips.text_zh: Compute 先係最值得投資嘅嘢。無論係股票定實際 physical chips 都得。Semi、Nvidia 嗰啲值得睇。Neocloud 只係 reseller，自己冇 product 同 software，風險好高。AI 可能連 software 都食埋。Hyperscaler 都有風險。
clips.text_en_b1: Compute is the only thing worth investing in. This can mean stocks or physical chips, especially semiconductors and Nvidia. Neoclouds are mainly resellers without their own products or software. Software may also be risky because AI could replace it. Hyperscalers are risky too.
clips.text_en_b2: Compute is the most worthwhile investment, whether you buy semiconductor stocks or physical chips. Nvidia is certainly worth watching. However, neoclouds are primarily resellers with neither proprietary products nor their own software, which makes them considerably riskier. The broader AI trend could also undermine software companies by replacing conventional tools. Even hyperscalers aren’t immune, since their enormous infrastructure spending introduces substantial financial exposure.
clips.text_en_c1: Compute is the only asset category that seems genuinely worth investing in, whether you buy semiconductor stocks, Nvidia, or the physical chips themselves. Neoclouds, by contrast, are largely resellers rather than companies that develop proprietary products or software, which exposes investors to greater operational and business risk. Even software is not automatically safe, since capable AI systems may absorb functionality that conventional applications currently provide. Hyperscalers offer more infrastructure and scale, but they carry their own financial and strategic uncertainties. The underlying argument is that the infrastructure on which AI runs may be the most durable bet.
clips.text_en_c2: Compute, in the poster’s view, is the only asset class genuinely worth backing, whether one acquires exposure through semiconductor stocks or physical chips. Nvidia and other semiconductor names are therefore the obvious points of focus. By contrast, neoclouds are dismissed as little more than resellers: they possess neither proprietary products nor a defensible software stack, which leaves them exposed to considerable risk. Even the software layer is not necessarily safe, since capable AI systems may absorb much of the functionality that traditional applications currently monetise. Hyperscalers, despite their scale and resources, are not immune either; the suggestion is that owning the compute infrastructure offers the cleanest route to durable AI-era returns.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ argument for owning semiconductor and compute assets rather than software.

clips.text_zh: 我間公司畀每個 developer 一個每月 $100 嘅 Claude seat，但每個 dev 每月用超過 $5,000 tokens。請問 Anthropic 點樣 sustain 呢個模式？靠AI續命，最後可能連老細都唔要。
clips.text_en_b1: My company pays for a $100 monthly Claude seat for every developer. However, each developer uses more than $5,000 worth of tokens every month. Explain how this can be sustainable for Anthropic. The high usage creates doubt about the long-term business model.
clips.text_en_b2: My company provides every developer with a Claude seat costing $100 per month, but each developer consumes more than $5,000 worth of tokens monthly. How can Anthropic possibly sustain that usage pattern? As developers rely more heavily on AI, the company may struggle to support them without charging considerably more. Although AI is keeping the business alive for now, it could eventually make even senior management redundant.
clips.text_en_c1: My company provides every developer with a Claude seat costing $100 per month, yet each individual consumes more than $5,000 worth of tokens annually. It is difficult to see how Anthropic can sustain that imbalance unless prices fall, usage is rationed, or enterprise discounts conceal the underlying cost. The figures also raise broader questions about whether per-seat pricing remains viable once intensive users generate unpredictable expenses. If AI-assisted development continues to accelerate token consumption, customers may eventually question whether conventional seats should be bundled differently. For now, the business model appears to depend on demand growing faster than usage costs.
clips.text_en_c2: Our company provides every developer with a Claude seat costing $100 per month, yet each individual consumes tokens worth more than $5,000 in a typical month. That discrepancy appears difficult to reconcile with sustainable unit economics, and it is not obvious how Anthropic can support the arrangement without losses becoming untenable. The burden of usage rests with the provider, whereas the employee receives a fixed corporate seat and effectively operates a personal AI utility at no marginal cost. If this pattern becomes standard among companies, AI may sustain itself only by cannibalising both software revenue and, eventually, the roles of senior managers themselves, leaving many businesses dependent on a technology whose appetite grows faster than its invoices.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ thread questioning Claude’s subscription economics when token usage is far higher.

clips.text_zh: 中東戰爭令 gas prices 升溫，power grid outages 嘅機會又增加咗。到時你架 Tesla 充唔到電，個 cyclist 就笑咗。咁你點解唔買部單車？睇晒成個 cost-benefit 啦。
clips.text_en_b1: Gas prices are increasing because of wars in the Middle East. Power grid outages are also becoming more likely, so your precious Tesla may not charge. Then the cyclist gets the last laugh. Why do you not own a bike? Consider the cost and benefits.
clips.text_en_b2: Wars in the Middle East are pushing gas prices upward, while the likelihood of power-grid outages is also increasing. Once the electricity supply becomes unstable, your precious Tesla may not be able to recharge properly. Then the cyclist really does get the last laugh. Considering the combined costs and benefits, owning a bicycle seems far more sensible, doesn’t it? Reliability starts to matter when fuel and charging become unpredictable.
clips.text_en_c1: War in the Middle East is pushing gasoline prices upward, while the likelihood of power-grid outages is also increasing. If supply chains and electricity networks become less reliable, even a carefully maintained Tesla may be unable to recharge when its owner needs it most. Under those conditions, the cyclist would have the last laugh: a simple bicycle requires neither fuel nor access to a functioning charging network. That does not make every car economically irrational, but it strengthens the case for evaluating transport choices against the full cost-benefit picture. Convenience has a price, and increasingly, that price includes resilience.
clips.text_en_c2: As warfare in the Middle East pushes petrol prices upward, the likelihood of power-grid failures has increased in parallel, creating two separate strains on household finances. More expensively, an electric vehicle may prove impossible to recharge precisely when mobility is needed most, leaving its owner dependent on infrastructure that remains conspicuously vulnerable. The cyclist, whose bicycle requires neither fuel nor a functioning charging network, consequently has the last laugh. If EVs are to represent a rational alternative to conventional cars, their appeal cannot rest solely on lower operating costs; buyers must also weigh whether their benefits genuinely outweigh the exposure to volatile energy markets and increasingly unreliable electricity supplies.
clips.source_hint: A /pol/ post linking war-driven fuel prices, grid outages, EVs, and bicycles.

clips.text_zh: Whitepill thread：hot cocoa 係最好嘅 pre-workout。任何人都可以開始 lifting，唔需要以前做過運動。六個月內可以逃出 skinnyfat mode。少過一年，啲人就會 notice 你開始 lift。Beginner programming 簡單到爆。
clips.text_en_b1: A whitepill thread says hot cocoa is the best pre-workout. Anyone can start lifting, without previous sports experience. You can escape skinnyfat mode in less than six months. People may notice your lifting within one year. Beginner programming is easy, and simple nutrition works.
clips.text_en_b2: This whitepill thread argues that hot cocoa is the best pre-workout, and honestly, why not? Anybody can begin lifting without any previous sporting experience. With consistent training and straightforward nutrition, you can escape skinnyfat mode in less than six months. Within a year, other people will probably start noticing that you lift. Most importantly, beginner programming is extremely simple, so there’s little reason to feel intimidated.
clips.text_en_c1: This whitepill thread presents hot cocoa as the best possible pre-workout, an encouragingly simple solution that anyone can adopt. You do not need a background in sport or weightlifting to begin training with basic beginner programming. With sensible resistance exercise, consistent nutrition, and enough time, you could escape the so-called skinny-fat phase in under six months. Once you have trained for a year, other people may begin to notice the changes in your physique and strength. Although no shortcut can replace sustained effort, the genuinely encouraging point is that beginner routines can be straightforward while still delivering measurable progress.
clips.text_en_c2: In this whitepill thread, hot cocoa is promoted as the ideal pre-workout ritual, an encouragingly harmless alternative to elaborate supplements that can rarely justify their price. No athletic pedigree is required: anyone with basic instructions and sufficient resolve can begin lifting, regardless of whether they have exercised before. With consistent training, the poster confidently claims, a newcomer can escape the so-called skinnyfat phase in under six months, while noticeable changes in strength and physique may become evident to other people within a year. The underlying programme for beginners is deliberately straightforward, since complex routines tend to intimidate rather than sustain participation. Simple nutrition, uncomplicated programming and gradual progress provide a notably more accessible route to results.
clips.source_hint: A /fit/ beginner whitepill about lifting, diet, and building a physique.

clips.text_zh: Yuru Camp rewatch。好嘅 Yuru Thursday to you too，anon！我哋完咗第一季，過咗幾舒服嘅時間。而家播 bonus content，包括三個 special。Relax 一下先，唔使急住估住下一步。
clips.text_en_b1: Yuru Camp rewatch, and a good Yuru Thursday to you too, anon. We finished season one and had a comfortable time. Now we are watching the bonus content from the first season. The discussion includes three specials: Heya Camp Episode 0, Tall Tale Camp, and Survival Camp.
clips.text_en_b2: It’s time for a Yuru Camp rewatch, and a good Yuru Thursday to you too, anon. We’ve just finished season one and had a thoroughly relaxing time. Now we’re moving on to the first season’s bonus content, which includes three specials: Heya Camp Episode 0, Tall Tale Camp, and Survival Camp. There’s no need to rush or predict what comes next, so let’s take it easy for a while.
clips.text_en_c1: It is time for a Yuru Camp rewatch, and a good Yuru Thursday to you too, anon. Having finished the first season, we had such a relaxed and pleasant experience that moving on felt unnecessary. We are now watching the bonus material associated with season one, including three specials: Heya Camp Episode 0, Tall Tale Camp, and Survival Camp. There is no need to rush or speculate about what comes next when the extra episodes provide a comfortable opportunity to revisit familiar characters and quieter moments. For now, the plan is simply to settle in and enjoy them.
clips.text_en_c2: A Yuru Camp rewatch is under way, with the thread offering a genial “Yuru Thursday” greeting to fellow enthusiasts, anon. Having completed the first season, the participants enjoyed an unhurried and thoroughly comfortable run, and have now moved on to its supplementary material. The bonus content comprises three specials: Heya Camp Episode 0, Tall Tale Camp and Survival Camp. Rather than speculating impatiently about what comes next, the thread adopts the series’ relaxed philosophy, savouring the remaining material at a leisurely pace. In a culture accustomed to relentless franchising and immediate sequel announcements, this deliberate pause is itself part of the appeal.
clips.source_hint: An /a/ rewatch thread for Yuru Camp’s first-season bonus episodes.

clips.text_zh: Grim news：而家新出嘅 Steam games 有 50% 用 AI。分析咗 63,000 幾款由 2024 年開始發布嘅 game，2024 年初只有 1.7%  disclose AI use。靠AI續命，而家連遊戲都係。
clips.text_en_b1: Almost half of all new games released on Steam in October 2026 used AI-generated content. An analysis covered more than 63,000 games released since January 2024. Valve introduced mandatory AI disclosures in January 2024, when the reported rate was only 1.7 percent.
clips.text_en_b2: Grim news for the games industry: around half of the new titles appearing on Steam are now using AI. An analysis examined more than 63,000 games released from January 2024 onwards, revealing a dramatic rise in adoption. Valve introduced mandatory AI disclosures in January 2024, when the reported rate was only 1.7 percent. AI is keeping countless projects alive, although it now seems to be spreading through the entire games market.
clips.text_en_c1: Some grim news for the Steam platform: an analysis of more than 63,000 games released since January 2024 suggests that almost half of the new titles appearing in October 2026 used AI-generated content. Valve introduced mandatory AI disclosure in January 2024, when the reported rate among new releases was only 1.7 percent. Although the figures do not explain how the AI was used, the scale of the increase indicates that generative tools have rapidly entered ordinary game development. What began as a marginal practice now appears close to standard practice, raising fresh questions about disclosure, creative labour, and the direction of the industry.
clips.text_en_c2: The news is grim for anyone who believes games remain a predominantly human craft: an analysis suggests that almost half of the new titles released on Steam in October 2026 contain AI-generated content. The dataset encompasses more than 63,000 games published since January 2024, allowing the trend to be traced over time. Valve introduced mandatory disclosure of AI use in January 2024, when only 1.7 percent of releases reportedly declared such involvement. The subsequent trajectory is strikingly steep, indicating that an initially marginal practice has become a substantial feature of the marketplace within barely two and a half years. What began as an occasional production shortcut now appears embedded in the industry’s standard release pipeline.
clips.source_hint: A /v/ post reporting the rising share of Steam games using AI-generated content.
